company_name: Compagnie Générale des Établissements Michelin SCA

inputs.share_count_basis: 677.639m shares outstanding at 30 June 2026 (687.606m issued less 9.967m treasury, H1-2026 interim note 11 share table) plus ~1.5m estimated dilution from performance shares, the only potentially dilutive instrument (FY2025 URD note 15). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would double-count. The EUR 453m of the EUR 753m buyback programme still to execute at 30 June is stripped from net debt and NOT removed from the count, which keeps the two consistent (buybacks are value-neutral in this model).
inputs.net_debt_basis: Michelin-defined net debt at 30 June 2026 EUR 4,547m (H1-2026 interim note 8.2) LESS lease liabilities EUR 964m (702 LT + 262 ST; leases are charged as an operating cost in the flows, treatment B) LESS the EUR 453m financial liability recognised for the unexecuted remainder of the buyback programme (interim note 8.3) = EUR 3,130m. total_debt = 7,957 - 964 - 453 = 6,540 (bonds 4,827, bank/other 1,353, NEU CP 750, derivatives 63, less buyback liability). cash = cash & equivalents 2,891 + cash-management financial assets 395 + borrowing collateral 25 + derivative assets 99 = 3,410, the same components Michelin nets in its own definition.
inputs.reported_fcf_basis: FY2025 net cash from operating activities 3,819 less gross purchases of intangibles and PP&E 2,017 (URD note 10). Michelin's own 'free cash flow before M&A' of 2,126 additionally adds back flows on cash-management assets and other non-current financial assets; not used.
inputs.last_fcf_basis: reported_fcf 1,802 - SBC 61 - interest_income 0 - lease cash 333 (lease principal 280 + lease interest 53, FY2025 URD cash-flow statement and note 9.1) = 1,408. Lease cash is deducted because lease liabilities are excluded from net debt (treatment B).
inputs.interest_income_note: Michelin is a net-debt company (ND/segment EBITDA 0.5x at Dec 2025, ~1.9x at June 2026 after dividend, buyback and M&A). FY2025 interest income on cash of EUR 104m is netted inside 'cost of net debt' below segment EBITDA, so it never enters the component build; no adjustment and no cash is double-counted.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 URD segment reconciliation, 'Share-based payments - current service cost' EUR 61m (ML.PA_Annual_FY2025.txt:24027; FY2024 also 61, FY2023 30, FY2022 20). Performance shares are settled from treasury shares; no net-share-settlement tax line exists, so EquityAwardTaxes = 0 and the combined figure equals the P&L charge.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing outflow EUR 668m (22.96m shares bought, 22.92m cancelled). H1 2026: EUR 300m executed (9.99m shares) of a EUR 753m programme; EUR 453m remainder recognised as a financial liability and stripped from net_debt here. The company is a consistent repurchaser, so the flat count is funded, not a convention.
inputs.price_note: Euronext Paris regular close (Friday 23 Oct 2026); not an after-hours print. 52-week range 26.90-35.72.
inputs.wacc_rationale: EUR flows discounted at a EUR-built rate: 10y OAT ~3.4%, ERP 5.5%, beta ~1.0 (five-year vs CAC 40) -> cost of equity ~8.9%; pre-tax cost of debt ~3.5% (2025 bond coupons 3.0-3.6%), 25% tax -> 2.6% after tax; market-value weights ~85% equity / 15% debt -> WACC 7.96%, rounded to 8.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality is priced in the flows and the weights, not stacked into the discount rate (adaptations rule f).
inputs.lease_treatment: B - leases as operating cost. Full lease cash (FY2025 principal 280 + interest 53 = 333, 1.28% of revenue) is charged inside the flows via lease_cost_pct_path = 1.3%; lease liabilities (EUR 964m at 30 June 2026) are excluded from net debt; D&A used for the tax EBIT is ex right-of-use depreciation (FY2025 total D&A 2,036 less ROU amortisation 245 = 1,791 = 6.9% of revenue, URD note 13).
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are EUR 4m of equity and EUR 4m of FY2025 profit; immaterial, no deduction.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical: industrials'), with the owner-fcf-adaptations applied: EUR-built WACC, single lease treatment (B), excluded-income/matching-asset rule (equity-accounted investments added in the bridge because their income is outside segment EBITDA), risk charged once. EBITDA margin path is an OWNER EBITDA: Michelin's segment EBITDA (17.9% of revenue in FY2025, 19.7% in FY2024, 19.1% ten-year average ex-2020) less ~1.3pp for the cash items the 'segment' measure excludes but shareholders pay every year - restructuring cash (430 in FY2025, 246 in FY2024), employee-benefit payments in excess of expense (108) and other non-recurring operating cash (URD note 10 'Other operating income and expenses (cash) and changes in provisions' 473 in FY2025, 246 in FY2024). Calibration: FY2025 drivers (17.9-1.3 = 16.6% owner EBITDA, 0.23% SBC, 1.3% lease, 6.9% D&A, 25% tax, 7.76% capex, zero working capital) reproduce unlevered owner FCF of ~EUR 1.35bn against the actual 1,408 levered owner FCF, which included a +273 working-capital inflow and -51 net interest; the gap is the working-capital windfall, deliberately not carried forward. Working capital capture is NEGATIVE (-15% of the revenue change): inventories 5.1bn + receivables 3.5bn exceed trade payables 3.3bn by ~20% of sales, so growth consumes cash. Capex uses Michelin's gross purchases (post-FY2022 definition); the pre-FY2022 'net capital spending' series is not like-for-like and is not used as an anchor. FY2026 is year 1: reported revenue guided roughly flat-to-down (H1 -2.6% reported, +0.5% at constant FX/scope, EUR/USD +7%), FCF before M&A guided above EUR 1.6bn, segment operating income growth at iso-FX/scope. SBC is 0.23% of revenue, so the house/street band is near-collapsed but not zero; band_position is computed, not nulled.
inputs.equity_bridge_note: See equity_bridge. Equity-accounted investments (TBC Corporation US retail JV and others) are added at FY2025 book value because their dividends (EUR 113m received in 2025, EUR 88m from TBC in April 2026) are not in an EBITDA-based flow. Tex Tech Industries (USD 491m, closed 2 July 2026, after the balance-sheet date) is deducted at ~EUR 420m (EUR/USD ~1.17 at the July close); its revenue is small and folded into the base growth path rather than modelled separately, which is conservative.

equity_bridge.item: Investments in equity-accounted companies at book (TBC Corp and others)
equity_bridge.note: FY2025 URD statement of financial position, note 14; income excluded from segment EBITDA so the asset is added (matching-asset rule)

equity_bridge.item: Tex Tech Industries acquisition closed 2 July 2026, post balance-sheet
equity_bridge.note: USD 491m per H1-2026 interim 1.6 'Evenements recents', converted at ~1.17; not in the 30 June net debt

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment anchored on the FY2016-FY2025 revenue CAGR of 2.4% and management's flat 2026 tire-market outlook; the 5-year figures all start from the FY2020 COVID trough and overstate trend, the 3-year figures start from the FY2022 price-inflation peak and understate it
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 7.4% diverges >30% from revenue 5yr CAGR 4.9% and from EPS 5yr CAGR 21.6%; both 5yr series are distorted by the FY2020 base (revenue 20,469, EPS 0.88). Equity 3yr CAGR 1.8% is depressed by EUR 1.17bn of buybacks and FX translation losses, not by weak earnings.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC less lease cash). 3yr owner-FCF CAGR is undefined because FY2022 owner FCF was negative (-443: reported -110, SBC 20, lease ~313) on a EUR 1.9bn working-capital build during the 2022 raw-material and inventory spike. 5yr: FY2020 ~1,693 (1,997 - 14 - ~290) to FY2025 1,408 = -3.6%/yr, versus reported FCF -2.0%/yr: SBC quadrupled (14 -> 61) and lease cash grew faster than cash flow over the period, though both remain small relative to a EUR 1.4bn base.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 -1.0% reported: H1 -2.6% (FX), H2 helped by Cooley/Flexitallic/Tex Tech consolidation and a softer EUR comparison; FY2027-29 +3% = flat-to-+1% tire volumes, +1.5-2% price/mix from the 18-inch+ mix-up, ~0.5pt Polymer Composite growth; fading to 2% nominal by FY2033.
base.margin_rationale: Owner EBITDA (segment EBITDA less ~1.3pp recurring restructuring/other cash). FY2026 17.3% = segment EBITDA ~18.6% (H1 19.1%, H2 seasonally lower, raw-material lag) less 1.3pp; recovers to the ten-year mid-cycle 18.0% (segment ~19.3%) by FY2030 as Tuscaloosa and European footprint restructuring complete. No credit for the Michelin in Motion 2030 margin ambition beyond mid-cycle.
base.capex_rationale: Gross purchases of intangibles and PP&E: FY2025 7.8%, FY2024 8.3%, FY2023 8.0%; H1 2026 695m annualises to ~7.2% as the competitiveness programme winds down. D&A ex-ROU 6.9% implies ~0.3-0.4pt of net investment, consistent with low-single-digit growth.
base.tax_rationale: Cash taxes 593/806/776 (FY2025/24/23) against a Group ETR that has averaged ~23%; 25% on unlevered EBIT is slightly above the ETR because interest is not deducted in the component build and France's statutory rate is 25.8%.
base.terminal_rationale: Gordon at 8%/2% implies 17x FCF; capped at 15x, the multiple a cyclical, capital-intensive industrial has historically been granted (Michelin's own EV/FCF has ranged ~10-16x). The cap binds in the base case.

bull.rationale: OE cycle turns in FY2027 (North American Class 8 and European passenger OE recover), EU anti-dumping duties hold Chinese import share in Europe, Polymer Composite Solutions compounds at high single digits off its ~EUR 1.4bn base, and restructuring takes owner EBITDA to 19% (segment ~20.3%, the FY2021/FY2024 level). Capex eases to 7.0% once the footprint programme ends.

bear.rationale: H2 2026 OE weakens further and the flagged EUR 400m raw-material inflation lands before pricing catches up; Chinese Tier 2/3 and EV-OE share gains cap price/mix at ~1%/yr, so revenue grows 1.5% nominal; owner EBITDA settles at 16% (segment ~17.3%, below the FY2025 trough-year 17.9%) as restructuring becomes permanent; capex stays at 7.5% to defend the footprint. Solvency is not in question (ND/EBITDA ~1x), so the bear is margin compression, not distress.

scenario_narratives.base: Michelin stays the #1 premium tire maker in a flat-volume market: FY2026 revenue dips ~1% on FX with segment operating income up at constant scope, as guided; FY2027-29 revenue grows ~3% nominal from 18-inch+ mix, modest pricing and the Polymer Composite bolt-ons; owner EBITDA margin recovers from the FY2025 trough (17.9% segment, 16.6% owner) to the ten-year mid-cycle (~19.3% segment, 18.0% owner) by FY2030 as Tuscaloosa and the European footprint programme complete; capex normalises to ~7.2% of sales; growth consumes working capital. Terminal value is bound by the 15x cap, not Gordon.
scenario_narratives.bull: The OE cycle turns in 2027 (NA Class 8 trucks, European passenger OE), EU anti-dumping duties on Chinese passenger tires protect European price/mix, China replacement share gains and EV tire wear lift volumes, and Polymer Composite Solutions compounds at high single digits into aerospace, energy and defense. Owner EBITDA reaches 19% (segment ~20.3%, the FY2021/FY2024 level) and capex eases to 7.0% once the restructuring programme ends; the market grants a 16x exit on a less cyclical mix.
scenario_narratives.bear: Chinese Tier 2/3 tires and Chinese EV-OE fitments permanently compress price/mix; the Western OE downturn extends through 2027 with no recovery catalyst; the flagged EUR 400m raw-material inflation hits before pricing responds; restructuring charges prove recurring rather than one-off. Revenue grows 1.5% nominal and owner EBITDA settles at 16% - below even the FY2025 trough. Balance-sheet risk is low (ND/EBITDA ~1x even after the 2026 dividend, buyback and M&A), so this is a margin and multiple (13x) story, not a solvency one.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Symmetric 25/50/25 rather than the house 15/50/35. Bear weight raised from 15% because the two highest-severity risks in the Analysis (Chinese low-cost competition, depressed Western OE demand) are already in motion and the FY2025/H1 2026 numbers sit at a trough with no visible OE catalyst; bull weight cut from 35% because the bull case needs three independent things (OE recovery, anti-dumping protection holding price/mix, Polymer Composite scaling) to go right together. No going-concern or covenant risk, so bear is not pushed higher.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Michelin is valued as a mature, capital-intensive cyclical on a strict owner-FCF basis: segment EBITDA is haircut for the restructuring and employee-benefit cash the company excludes from its own measure, leases are expensed in full, SBC is charged, working capital consumes cash with growth, and the terminal multiple is capped at 15x FCF rather than letting an 8%/2% Gordon value (17x) run. The FY2025 base year is below mid-cycle (segment margin 17.9% vs a 19.1% ten-year average), so the base case recovers margin rather than extrapolating the trough, but takes no credit for the Michelin in Motion 2030 ambition beyond mid-cycle. Net debt is the 30 June 2026 figure (post dividend, post EUR 300m buyback, post Cooley/Flexitallic), with the unexecuted EUR 453m buyback liability stripped and Tex Tech deducted; equity-accounted investments are added at book because their income is outside the flows.
key_risks_to_valuation: Owner EBITDA margin assumption: each 1pp of terminal margin is worth roughly EUR 3-4/share; the bear case's 16% is below any year since 2016 except 2020, the bull's 19% has been reached twice in ten years

Restructuring recurrence: the model charges ~1.3% of revenue every year; if Michelin's cash restructuring genuinely ends after Tuscaloosa (2028), value is understated by ~EUR 3/share; if it runs higher than 2025's EUR 430m, overstated
FX translation: ~40% of revenue is USD; a 7% EUR appreciation took ~3pts off reported FY2026 H1 growth and the model's EUR flows carry that exposure unhedged
Terminal cap: 15x binds in the base case; a buyer granting Gordon (17x) adds ~EUR 2/share, a buyer granting 13x (bear) removes ~EUR 2
Working-capital sign: 2022 showed a EUR 1.9bn build on a raw-material spike; the -15% capture assumes orderly growth, not another inventory shock

Net-debt vintage: 30 June 2026 is after the annual dividend (EUR 944m) and seasonally peaked inventories; December net debt is typically EUR 1-2bn lower, so the mid-year anchor is conservative by ~EUR 1.5-2.5/share relative to a year-end anchor
